published_statement: (a) FO p.10, Theorem 4.2 (verbatim from cache): 'Let omega_2^0 be the two-point function of a reference Hadamard state for the non-minimally coupled scalar field with coupling constant xi in [0, 1/4], defined on a globally hyperbolic spacetime with smooth metric. Furthermore, let gamma be a time-like geodesic parametrised in proper time tau and let f in D(R,R). On the set of Hadamard states, we then find (rho_quant o gamma)(f^2) >= -Q_xi(f), (44) where Q_xi(f) = Qt_A^xi(f) 1 + xi(:Phi^2: o gamma)(Q_B[f]) + xi(:Phi^2: o gamma)(Q_C^xi[f]) (45) ... Q_B[f](tau) = 2(d_tau f)^2 (47), Q_C^xi[f](tau) = f^2 (R_mn gamma^m gamma^n - (1/2)(1-4xi)R) (48). Furthermore Qt_A^xi(f) and Q_B[f] are non-negative.' (b) FFKP p.18: 'Theorem IV.1. Let f be any real-valued test function compactly supported in a small sampling domain. Let l^mu be a null vector field defined in the neighbourhood of support of f. Then, for all Hadamard states psi <:rho_n:(f^2)>_psi >= -2 INT_D d^n alpha/(2pi)^n ((Q x Q)W_0)_kappa(fbar_alpha, f_alpha) - xi <:phi^2:(Q[f])>_psi, (72) where W_0 is the two-point function of the reference Hadamard state psi_0 and Q = l^mu nabla_mu', with (69b) Q[f] = nabla_mu nabla_nu (l^mu l^nu f^2) + (1/2) R_mn l^mu l^nu f^2; 'unlike those two inequalities [FO, Fewster-Kontou], the QEI derived holds for any value of the coupling constant xi'; 'as this bound is derived by discarding positive terms we do not expect it to be optimal'.

COPIED DISCREPANCY (carried from the source, not introduced by the tree) at qeihps.py:98-99: the tree displays FFKP's Q[f] = nabla nabla(l l f^2) + (1/2) R_mn l^m l^n f^2 verbatim from (69b) (check T1d). FFKP's own stress tensor (9) -- shown conserved here on an FRW metric (N2, residual 1e-166) -- null-contracts to T_ll = (1-2xi)(l.dphi)^2 - 2xi[phi l l dd phi - (1/2)R_ll phi^2] (N1b), whereas (13) prints '+ (1/2) R_ll phi^2' inside the bracket: (9)_ll - (13) = 2 xi R_ll phi^2 exactly (N1). Carried through the Leibniz/integration-by-parts step, (9) gives Q_true[f] = nabla_mu nabla_nu(l^mu l^nu f^2) - R_ll f^2, verified here as a POINTWISE divergence identity f^2 T_ll = f^2 (l.dphi)^2 - xi phi^2 Q_true[f] + div V on FRW with an explicit null field (N3b, residual 4e-165); the printed +1/2 leaves exactly -(3/2) xi R_ll f^2 phi^2 (N3c, N3d). (13) as printed would give +1; (61) as extracted shows +1 inside -2xi(...), i.e. +2; (64)/(69b)/(72) print +1/2 -- consistent with none. This is a DISCREPANCY IN v1 AS EXTRACTED, not a refutation: the journal version is unread, and no state violating the printed (72) is exhibited (the bound is not sharp). Inert for the tree: every 'Q[f]'/'R_ll' in qeihps.py is the docstring display at lines 98-99 (T1e); nothing evaluates it. It would be live if (72) were ever evaluated on HPS, where R_ll != 0 on any open supp f (audits/2309.10848-thmiv.1.json C4b: -226800 pi^2 l^2 + O(l^4)).

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested for this composite. Neither theorem has an empirical input, so there is no measured datum either set of authors could have lacked, and none has moved (data_at_publication). Evidence against M's hypothesis for these results: FO Thm 4.2's range and classical skeleton re-derive (F1 here; 22/22 in the component script), and FFKP's proof structure re-derives (N5) -- nothing is refuted. Evidence FOR a weaker form of M's suspicion ('incomplete or inaccurate', not 'lacked data'): FFKP v1's printed curvature coefficient in Q[f] (+1/2) is not the one its own conserved stress tensor (9) produces (-1; N1-N3). That is an internal algebraic discrepancy, not missing data, and it is invisible in every application FFKP make (Minkowski DSNEC/SNEC, R_mn = 0) -- which plausibly explains why it was not caught; it matters only where R_ll != 0 and xi != 0, i.e. exactly the curved use Kontou requests for HPS. What IS lacking -- for everyone, then and now -- is the INPUT to evaluate either bound on HPS: a reference Hadamard state (FO's omega_0, FFKP's W_0) on HPS's metric, <:Phi^2:> in HPS's state, and a proof that HPS's AHS-approximated state is Hadamard. HPS printed none; Kontou 2024 names the test and supplies none; neither later paper read here supplies them. Having the corrected coefficient changes no tree verdict: the refusal (OPEN, not evaluable) stands on the missing inputs.
grade_evidence: Both components READ at source (cached alphaXiv extractions; Theorem 4.2 and Theorem IV.1 re-read verbatim this stage) and the composite's own conclusion -- both apply in form to HPS's xi = 1/6 field, neither evaluable, OPEN -- is faithful and computed (T1a, T1b, T1f), so the TREE'S VERDICT STANDS. The grade is NARROWED, not STANDS, because the external results as the tree carries them hold on a smaller class than stated: (1) FO Thm 4.2 requires a globally hyperbolic smooth spacetime, and the tree drops that hypothesis from FO's form test (FORM_TAGS[FO] = {xi, geodesic}, qeihps.py:402-403; T1c) while carrying it for FS and FFKP -- restorable only LOCALLY ('applies in form locally'); (2) FFKP Thm IV.1's printed right side, with Q[f] = nabla nabla(l l f^2) + (1/2) R_ll f^2 (copied at qeihps.py:98-99), is supported by the paper's own conserved stress tensor (9) only where R_mn l^m l^n = 0 on supp f or xi = 0; in general (9) gives Q_true = nabla nabla(l l f^2) - R_ll f^2 (N1-N3, pointwise identity machine-checked on FRW to 4e-165, printed form off by exactly -(3/2) xi R_ll f^2 phi^2), and HPS's throat neighbourhood has R_ll != 0. This is recorded as a DISCREPANCY in v1 as extracted -- NOT a refutation and NOT to be quoted as an error in SciPost Phys. 16, 119 until that version is read; no violating state is shown, and the theorem survives with Q_true (N5). Not WRONG: nothing in either source is refuted by a counterexample, and nothing the tree computes is contradicted. Not DATA-DEPENDENT: no datum enters. Not OPEN: both statements were read and every finite claim checked; only the journal version of FFKP and a fresh literature search were unavailable (quota / proxy), which bears on item (2)'s status in print, not on the computation.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: (i) the tree adds FO's global-hyperbolicity hypothesis to FORM_TAGS[FO] with the local restriction named (as it does for FS), AND (ii) FFKP's SciPost version (or a v2) is read and shows (12)/(13)/(69b) corrected to the coefficient consistent with (9), with the tree's display at qeihps.py:98-99 then updated or marked -- or an error is found in checks N1-N3 (re-run; exact differentiation evaluated at 30 digits). To WRONG for FFKP (72) as printed: an explicit Hadamard state on a background with R_ll != 0 on supp f violating the printed bound -- not attempted and not implied, since the bound is not sharp. To OPEN: the journal version restates Theorem IV.1 with a different Q[f] whose derivation cannot be checked here. The tree's O5 refusal would change only if a reference Hadamard state and <:Phi^2:> on HPS were supplied (then both become EVALUABLE, T1f) -- at which point the Q[f] coefficient becomes load-bearing.
